newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says to support bank over Iran loan.
newsitem.headline: Germany says to support bank over Iran loan.

text.p: The German Economics Ministry said on Saturday it would support a German bank in a dispute with a U.S. senator over refusing to withdraw a loan it granted to Iran's Offshore Engineering and Construction Company.
A ministry spokeswoman said the loan was an independent decision made by the Duesseldorf-based bank and that foreign influence would not be politically and legally acceptable.
A WestLB spokesman said earlier this week that the bank was not breaching any laws because trade finance deals were not covered by the 1996 Iran Libya Sanctions Act (ILSA).
WestLB belongs to a bank consortium that has lent the state-owned Iranian company $90 million. WestLB's share of the loan is $40 million.
The loan will be used to finance the supply of machinery and technical equipment by German, French and Belgian exporters to develop the Souroush oil field, according to WestLB.
In a letter sent last week to WestLB chief executive Friedel Neuber, New York Republican Senator Al D'Amato said the deal was a clear violation of ILSA.
D'Amato was a key author of the legislation, which imposes U.S. sanctions on any company that invests $40 million or more in a 12-month period in the petroleum sectors of Iran or Libya.

D'Amato said the scheme would be nothing more than an effort to wilfully circumvent ILSA and that any business deal that provided Iran with hard currency to develop its energy sector was regarded as a threat to U.S. national security.
He also said that if WestLB went ahead with the loan it would become a "pariah company known for supporting rogue states."
Plans for the loan have also been condemned by the German office of the National Council of Resistance of Iran.
